name: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd
title: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd - 541729 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: HDFC AMC Q2 FY27 shows steady AUM growth (avg AUM INR9.69tn, +10% YoY) and tight cost control, but active equity market share slipped to 11.1% and management offered no new numeric guidance.

triggers.label: Market share 11.5% best → 11.1%
triggers.quote: the best, I think, was 11.5%. And in this current quarter, it's 11.1%

triggers.label: Systematic flows softness from STP
triggers.quote: The softness we have noticed has come from STP.

triggers.label: New AIF Cat II and Cat III launches
triggers.quote: we launched 2 new AIFs, a Category II equity fund focused on private markets

triggers.label: SIP contributions record INR325bn
triggers.quote: monthly contributions reaching a new high of INR325 billion in September

red_flags.label: Systematic flows softness (STP pauses)
red_flags.quote: some of them paused these transfers

red_flags.label: Cost growth scrutiny; H1 expense up ~16%
red_flags.quote: there were some CSR expenses which were taken up in the first quarter

evasions.topic: Alternatives revenue target / INR100 crore timing
evasions.quote: we don't give guidance like this when will we reach a certain amount
We don't specify flow data category-wise for HDFC AMC.
Sir, we don't hazard a guess on anything that is in future.

summary.headline: HDFC AMC Q2 FY27: revenue from operations up 14% YoY to INR11.7 billion; operating profit up 16% to INR9.1 billion at 36 bps of AUM.
summary.overview: Quarterly average AUM rose 10% YoY and 4% QoQ to INR9.69 trillion, with equity-oriented AUM at 67.1% versus 57.5% for the industry. Revenue from operations was INR11.7 billion (+14% YoY), operating profit INR9.1 billion (+16%), and PBT INR9.8 billion (+12%). Reported PAT is not comparable YoY because the year-ago quarter had a INR468 million tax provision reversal. Management pushed alternatives, PMS and GIFT City as growth areas, and defended cost growth as a mix of routine costs and forward investment.

segments.name: Active equity
segments.commentary: Yield of 61 bps; overall equity yield 58 bps, with a marginal sequential rise attributed mainly to asset mix. Active equity AUM INR6.08 trillion at 12.7% share.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Yield about 28-29 bps. Debt AUM INR1.62 trillion, 13% market share.

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: Yield 13 bps. Liquid AUM INR860 billion, up 10% YoY.

segments.name: Alternatives and PMS
segments.commentary: Two new alternative funds launched: a Category II late-stage venture/growth fund and a first Category III fund; a Category II private equity fund (fund of funds) is fully committed to 13 GPs. EPFO fixed income mandate went live this quarter; management says AIF fees run 80-90 bps above equity MF fees. Share of non-MF revenue described as small.

segments.name: Passive and GIFT City
segments.commentary: Around 50 passive products; second-largest in index funds among retail-heavy categories. Six inbound and two outbound GIFT City funds.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give timelines for alternatives revenue (e.g., INR100 crore target).
New SIF (specialised investment fund) product launches expected over the next couple of quarters, after hiring two senior investment professionals.
Two new AIF launches in progress: Select Opportunities fund final-close process and Emerging Opportunities Category III fund fundraising continuing.
Management expects a steady CSR-related cost skew to unwind; asks investors to assess costs on a full-year basis.
FY27 non-cash ESOP expense expected at about INR79-80 crore.
capex_capacity: Cost commentary: investments in people (alternatives team of over 20 investment professionals; MF team about 40 versus 30 a couple of years back), investor servicing, operations, distribution, international and technology/AI.
Balance sheet cash deployed as seed capital for alternative platforms; Board has distributed almost all post-tax distributable cash profits over the last three years.
Systematic transactions 19 million in September (up from about 17 million in June); monthly SIP flows INR325 billion in September.
demand_pricing: Industry: equity-oriented net inflows INR1,161 billion in the quarter; 67th consecutive month of positive equity flows. Debt funds net outflows INR607 billion; liquid inflows INR457 billion; ETFs INR367 billion.
Systematic flows (SIP + STP) INR48 billion in September, up 6% YoY. Management says softness is in STP (paused by wealth managers when markets were choppy), while SIP-only market share rose.
Unique investors 17.7 million (28% penetration), added 3.2 million in last year versus industry 6.3 million. Live individual accounts 32 million, up from 26 million.

Market share in the quarter was 11.1% versus a prior best of 11.5% per an analyst; hybrid categories such as multi-asset, aggressive hybrid and equity savings saw share correction, with a new hybrid fund manager brought in.
Management said mid-cap fund is above INR1 lakh crore; small-cap fund about INR40,000 crore and ranked second or third in its category.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of sequential yield improvement and asset-wise yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Active equity 61 bps, overall equity 58 bps, debt 28-29 bps, liquid 13 bps. Improvement largely asset mix; not material.

qa_highlights.question: Alternatives revenue target and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give timelines; launched two new alternative funds and says the platform now works as full stack.

qa_highlights.question: Is SIP market share at risk from newer AMCs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident; SIP share has grown on track record, products, distribution and focus on SIPs, though competition is intense.

qa_highlights.question: Why is systematic flow share down in the last three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the comparison is not like-for-like; the softness is in STP, while SIP-only share rose. Systematic transactions rose from about 17 million to 19 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did staff and non-staff costs fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps tight cost control while investing in people, alternatives, international, digital and AI; no split of routine versus investment cost was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the equity yield gap versus peers due to product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields vary by fund size; TER falls as AUM rises, and three funds are above INR1 lakh crore. No yield guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 expense growth high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSR expenses were taken in Q1, skewing H1; asked investors to look at full-year costs.

risks_watch: Market share movement: 11.1% in the quarter with hybrid category share correction.
STP pauses in volatile markets could affect systematic flows.
Small-cap fund scale and flow share versus peers.
Cost growth: management points to forward investments in people, alternatives, international and technology.
Use of balance sheet cash for seed capital, with no buyback or special dividend indicated.
summary.management_tone: Confident and defensive on flows, market share and cost; management pushed back on several analyst framings. It declined to give numeric targets for alternatives, yield or cost, and pointed to full-year numbers instead.
key_quotes: If you strip out STP and look at only the SIP, our market share has actually gone up.
We watch every rupee we spend.

growth.why: No explicit numeric revenue guidance; management pushes alternatives, PMS and GIFT City with new AIF and SIF launches expected but no timelines for alternatives revenue, so backing is vague while the quarter showed revenue +14% and operating profit +16% YoY on 10% AUM growth.
